mainEntity.name: How do several words search?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every word typed must be in the verse, in any order: love neighbour finds the verses that have both. Add a word to narrow the answer; there is no need to type AND.

mainEntity.name: How do I search for an exact phrase?

acceptedAnswer.text: Put it in double quotes: "the good shepherd" finds those words together, in that order. Quoted and plain words mix: "good shepherd" sheep.

mainEntity.name: Why does bless also find blessed and blessing?

acceptedAnswer.text: A plain search matches anywhere inside a word, so bless finds bless, blessed, blessing and blessedness. That is usually what is wanted; switch on ab| at the end of the search field for whole words only.

mainEntity.name: How do I find a whole word only?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switch on ab| at the end of the search field. man then finds man but not manner or woman. A word ends where its letters, their marks and digits stop — so in Burmese, which writes words together, a whole word is one set off by a space or punctuation.

mainEntity.name: Does capitalisation matter in a search?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not unless Aa is switched on at the end of the search field. With Aa on, LORD finds the small-capital LORD of the Old Testament and not Lord.

mainEntity.name: Do accents and marks matter in a search?

acceptedAnswer.text: Accents on Latin letters are ignored, so elan finds élan. Marks in Burmese, Hebrew, Arabic and similar scripts are kept, because there they make a different word; type them as the translation writes them.

mainEntity.name: How do I search for a Strong's number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Type the number alone, like H430 or G26, where the translation carries Strong's numbers. The words tagged with it are found and highlighted. H1254 finds every sense of the number; H1254A only that one.

mainEntity.name: There are too many results — how do I narrow them?

acceptedAnswer.text: The counts at the top are exact, however many there are; the first 2,000 verses are listed. Add a word, quote a phrase, or choose where to search under the field — a testament, a section such as the Gospels, or chosen books.

mainEntity.name: What is a regular expression?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pattern that describes text rather than spelling it out. Switch on .* at the end of the search field and what is typed becomes a pattern. Letters still match themselves, so shepherd works as before; a few characters have a meaning of their own: . | ? * + ( ) [ ] { } ^ $ \. Each verse is searched on its own.

mainEntity.name: How do I find either of two words?

acceptedAnswer.text: Separate them with |: shepherd|sheep finds verses with either. Group a part with brackets to keep the rest in common: (good|great) shepherd.

mainEntity.name: How do I allow for two spellings?

acceptedAnswer.text: ? makes the character before it optional: Saviou?r finds Saviour and Savior. A choice of letters goes in square brackets: gr[ae]y finds grey and gray.

mainEntity.name: How do I match any letter, or any number of them?

acceptedAnswer.text: . is any one character; * repeats what is before it zero or more times, + one or more. s.t finds sat, set, sit; bless\p{L}* finds bless and every word that starts with it. \p{L} is a letter in any script, where \w is only a–z, 0–9 and _. Burmese and other scripts write vowels as marks beside the letters, so for a whole word there use [\p{L}\p{M}]+.

mainEntity.name: How do I say how many times something repeats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Braces give a count: \p{L}{12,} finds words of twelve letters or more, (holy, ){2} finds holy repeated. {3} is exactly three, {2,5} two to five.

mainEntity.name: How do I search for a character that has a meaning in a pattern?

acceptedAnswer.text: Put a backslash before it: \? is a question mark, \. a full stop, \( a bracket. \?$ finds the verses that end with a question.

mainEntity.name: How do I find a verse that starts or ends a certain way?

acceptedAnswer.text: ^ is the start of the verse and $ its end: ^And finds verses that begin with And; !$ those that end with an exclamation.

mainEntity.name: How do I find two words near each other?

acceptedAnswer.text: .{0,40} allows up to forty characters between them: faith.{0,40}love finds faith followed closely by love. For either order, give both: faith.{0,40}love|love.{0,40}faith.

mainEntity.name: How do I find a word said twice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Brackets capture what they match and \1 repeats it: ([\p{L}\p{M}]+),? \1 finds a word said twice in a row, such as Verily, verily or Holy, holy.

mainEntity.name: How do I find verses with one word and without another?

acceptedAnswer.text: A lookahead checks the whole verse without using it up: ^(?!.*hate).*love finds love in verses that do not also say hate.

mainEntity.name: How do I match whole words in a pattern?

acceptedAnswer.text: \b marks the edge of a word, but only of words written in a–z: \bman\b is right for English. For any script, look around for letters instead: (?<![\p{L}\p{M}])man(?![\p{L}\p{M}]). The ab| switch does not apply to patterns.

mainEntity.name: How do I find capitals, numerals or a script?

acceptedAnswer.text: \p{Lu} is a capital letter in any alphabet: with Aa on, \p{Lu}{3,} finds LORD. \p{N} is a numeral in any script — 12 and ၁၂ alike — and \d only 0–9. \p{Script=Myanmar} is a Burmese character, \p{Script=Hebrew} a Hebrew one.

mainEntity.name: My pattern says it cannot be searched — why?

acceptedAnswer.text: The pattern has a mistake, and the search says which: an unclosed bracket (Unterminated group), a * or + with nothing before it (Nothing to repeat), or a lone backslash at the end. Close the bracket or put a backslash before the character.
